openings.claim: An offset head with a pin-only guide might align the pin through small manual taps; the guide is predicted to keep contact on the pin while limiting unintended side force.
openings.discriminator: Predicts alignment without housing contact, with no claim of lower vibration than another device. Housing contact or an immobile pin defeats adequacy.
openings.probe: Proposed only: inspect a surrogate contact envelope, then attempt incremental alignment under varied friction.
openings.uncertainty: Guide clearance and required impulse remain unknown.

openings.claim: A powered pulse head might improve impulse-size control; a controlled actuator is predicted to reduce operator-dependent pulse variation.
openings.discriminator: Predicts lower pulse variation than manual tapping; equal variation defeats the advantage. Does not predict lower housing damage.
openings.probe: Proposed only after explicitly relaxing manual-actuation-only and establishing an actuator resource.
openings.uncertainty: Requires hard-constraint relaxation; actuator availability and vibration transmission remain unknown.

lineage.reason: Preserves declared fit and complete protected relation, test, and uncertainty.
Conditional fit preserved; unavailable within current manual-only constraints.

Declared fit violates: lubricating before tapping might reduce impulse through lower sliding resistance and easier alignment, but no-lubricant rejects it. Reduction is merely suggested; lubricant might have no effect under unspecified friction. Probe parked: no lubricant trial within this case. Impulse reduction, contamination effects, and compatibility remain unresolved.

decision: Consider D1 for hypothetical investigation toward moving the pin to its reference mark without housing damage. Enforce no housing contact, no lubricant addition, and manual actuation only. D2 requires explicit relaxation, currently unauthorized. All proposals are synthetic and untested; geometry/reference mark are hypothetical, friction unspecified, and no pin, housing, vibration measurements, usable equipment, or power source is supplied.
